questions.stem: Most important mechanism of methotrexate when used as a disease modifying anti-rheumatoid drug is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Inhibition of AICAR transformylase

  • Although methotrexate is inhibitor of dihydrofolic acid reductase (DHFRase) enzyme, however, inhibition of DHFR is not thought to be the main mechanism in treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis. Major mechanism of methotrexate in Rheumatoid Arthritis appears to be to increase extracellular adenosine levels. 
  • Methotrexate causes inhibition of enzymes involved in de novo purine synthesis. AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide)  transformylase  converts AICAR to 10-formyl AICAR and is directly inhibited by methotrexate. This leads to accumulation of AICAR that inhibits adenosine deaminase. So adenosine cannot be converted to inosine resulting in increase in level of adenosine. Adenosine is an important mediator of the anti-inflammatory effects of methotrexate.

 

 

  • Adenosine acts on A2A receptor and produces the following effects:
    • It inhibits superoxide anion generation in neutrophils and increases engulfment-mediated neutrophil function.
    • It promotes transition from M1 to M2 macrophages (M1 macrophages are pro-inflammatory and M2 macrophages have an anti-inflammatory effect) and inhibits cytokine expression.
    • It downregulates T cell activation and proliferation by inhibiting T cell receptor (TCR) triggered activation.
    • It may lead to development of T regulatory cells (Tregs) known to express both CD39 and CD73 that may decrease T cell activation.

questions.stem: Which of the following binds to viral envelope glycoprotein preventing the conformational changes required for the fusion of viral and cellular membranes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Enfuvirtide

 

Enfuvirtide, also known as T-20, is a medication used to treat HIV infection.

 

It works by binding to the viral envelope glycoprotein gp41, which is necessary for the fusion of the viral and cellular membranes during viral entry.

 

By binding to gp41, enfuvirtide prevents the conformational changes required for membrane fusion, thereby inhibiting viral entry into the host cell.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Abacavir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor, which blocks the reverse transcriptase enzyme required for HIV replication.

 

Option B. Indinavir is a protease inhibitor, which blocks the protease enzyme required for HIV maturation.

 

Option D. Oseltamivir is a medication used to treat influenza. It inhibits the neuraminidase enzyme, which is necessary for the release of newly formed viral particles from infected cells.

questions.stem: Ubrogepant is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. CGRP receptor antagonist

  • Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is a neuropeptide that acts in the trigeminovascular system and is believed to play an important role in pain transmission in migraine.
  • CGRP is produced in both peripheral and central neurons. It is a potent vasodilator and its level increases following migraine attack.
  • CGRP receptor antagonists (“Gepants”) does not vasoconstrictive effects, shows comparable efficacy, and has fewer adverse effects than triptans. As they do not cause vasoconstriction, they are safe to be used in patients with cardiovascular disease.
  • Currently, four monoclonal antibodies against CGRP are approved: (Given by s.c. injection)
    • Erenumab
    • Fremanezumab
    • Galcanezumab
    • Eptinezumab
       
  • Gepants are small molecule drugs which are effective at both relieving and treating migraine. Approved gepants are (given orally):
    • Ubrogepant
    • Rimegepant
    • Atogepant
       

Other options:

questions.stem: For overdose of several drugs, we can change the pH of the urine. Urine can be made alkaline for increasing the excretion of all of the following drugs except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Morphine

  • Acidic drugs (barbiturate, methotrexate, salicylate) are more ionized at alkaline urine and are not absorbed from renal tubules if the urine is alkaline, and their excretion in urine is increased. Therefore, alkalization of urine is done by NaHCO3 in the poisoning of acidic drugs.
  • For the same reason, acidification of urine is done by ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) in poisoning of basic drugs (morphine, amphetamines, quinine).
  • So, the question simply asks which of the following is a basic drug. Remember, the drugs ending with ‘ine’ are basic.


ore, alkalization of urine is done by NaHCO3 in the poisoning of acidic drugs.

questions.stem: Volume of distribution of a drug is 50 L and target plasma concentration of drug required is 5 mg/L. If 20% of orally administered drug reaches the systemic circulation, what will be the oral loading dose of this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans.  C. 1.25 g

 

Loading dose  = Target Cp x Vd

  • Target concentration (Cp) = 5 mg/L
  • Volume of distribution = 50 L
  • So, the loading dose is 50 x 5 = 250 mg
  • So, 250 g of drug is required by intravenous route. However, we want to give the drug by oral route, and F (Fraction of administered drug reaches systemic circulation) = 20% = 0.2
  • So, loading dose = 250 / 0.2 = 1250 mg = 1.25 g

questions.stemHtml: Given image shows the Log DRC of a drug alone (A) and in the presence of antagonists (B and C). Identify the type of antagonism shown in curve B and curve C?

options.label: C
options.text: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist

options.label: D
options.text: B is non-competitive an C is competitive antagonist

questions.answerText: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. B is competitive and C is non competitive antagonist

  • In competitive antagonism, the DRC shifts towards right i.e. potency decreases but efficacy remains same.
  • On the other hand, in case of non-competitive antagonism, the curve becomes flat ie potency remains same but efficacy decreases.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following gives the extent of drug absorption in plasma concentration vs time graph shown below in the figure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Area under the curve

 

PC vs Time Graph

  • After taking a drug, levels peak quickly then drop slowly as the drug is eliminated (cleared from the body) – every drug has its own absorption curve.
  • The highest concentration is called the Cmax.
  • The total exposure to drug over the dosing period is call the Area Under the Curve (AUC)
  • The time taken to get to the highest concentration is called the Tmax
  • The time taken to reduce the highest concentration by half (by 50%) is called a drug’s ‘half-life’ or T½.
  • It takes approximately 5 half-lives for a drug to be cleared to negligible levels, but in theory, tiny quantities can be in the body for much longer.
  • Tmax tell the rate of absorption of a drug whereas AUC tells the extent of absorption of a drug.

questions.stem: A patient presents to you with hypothyroidism and you want to prescribe oral thyroxine at a dose of 100 microgram (0.1 milligram) daily for 30 days. As an Indian medical intern, which of the following is the correct format for prescription of this drug?

options.label: A
options.text: Tablet Thyroxine 100 µg once a day orally for 30 days

options.label: B
options.text: Tablet Thyroxine 100 mcg OD orally for 30 days

options.label: C
options.text: Tablet Thyroxine .1 mg once a day orally for 30 days

options.label: D
options.text: Tablet Thyroxine 100 mcg once a day orally for 30 days

questions.answerText: Tablet Thyroxine 100 mcg once a day orally for 30 days
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Tablet Thyroxine 100 mcg once a day orally for 30 days

 

IMPORTANT POINTS REGARDING PRESCRIPTION WRITING:

  • Prescription is invalid without date and signature of the doctor.
  • Drug name should never been written in abbreviation form (e.g. never write PCM for paracetamol).
  • Abbreviations like OD, BD, HS etc should not be used in prescription. So, option B is incorrect.
  • Leading zeros should always be mentioned (e.g. 0.5 mg is correct but .5 mg is incorrect). So, option C is incorrect.
  • Trail zeros should never be written (e.g. 5 mg is correct but 5.0 is incorrect).
  • Microgram should be written as mcg not as µg. So, option A is incorrect.

questions.stemHtml: After eating a plant as shown in the figure below, A child presented to emergency in comatose state. The pupils were dilated and skin was dry. Body temperature is raised and heart rate is high. These signs and symptoms are similar to intake of which of the following substance?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Atropine

  • The plant shown in the figure is Dhatura stramomium. It is the source of atropine.
  • The characteristic features of atropine poisoning are:

D: Dry mouth and Delirium

H: Hyperthermia

A: Agitation

T: Tachycardia

U: Urinary

R: Retention

A: Accommodation lost (Mydriasis, Photophobia, Blurred Vision)

questions.stemHtml: Repeated administration of a drug, produces the following effect on blood pressure (as shown in the diagram). What is this phenomenon known as?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Tachyphylaxis

  • When repeated doses of a drug produce less response than original, it is called tachyphylaxis.
  • It is shown by indirectly acting sympathomimetic drugs like tyramine and ephedrine. 

Exact mechanism of this is not known, but it is assumed to be due to depletion of neurotransmitter in the synapse.

questions.stem: A hypertensive patient was on metoprolol treatment. Verapamil was added to the therapy of this patient. This can result in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Bradycardia with AV block

 

Ref: KDT 8th/160

  • Beta blockers like metoprolol depress the heart. They decrease the heart rate, conduction as well as contractility
  • Calcium channel  blockers like verapamil and diltiazem also depress the heart.
  • Beta blockers should never be combined with verapamil or diltiazem due to additive cardiac depression leading to severe bradycardia and AV block.


KDT 8th/160

questions.stem: A patient requires mild cholinomimetic stimulation following surgery. Physostigmine and bethanechol in small doses have significantly different effects on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Neuromuscular junction

  • Bethanechol acts on muscarinic receptors only whereas physostigmine increases Ach, thus can stimulate both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors,
  • Neuromuscular junction contains NM receptors, thus will be affected by physostigmine but not by bethanechol.
  • Gastric acid secretion, sweating and ureteral tone is regulated by muscarinic receptors, thus both physostigmine and bethanechol can work on these.

questions.stem: A child on formoterol inhaler for treatment of bronchial asthma may exhibit all of the following features except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Hypoglycemia (Ref: KDT 6/e p124)

  • β2 agonists are the inhaled bronchodilators used for the management of bronchial asthma.
  • Tremor is the dose related adverse effect of these drugs.
  • Hypokalemia is an important adverse effect of these agents. This happens because beta 2 agonists increase the increase the intracellular movement of K.
  • β2 agonists do not cause hypoglycemia, rather these increase blood sugar.


KDT 6/e p124)

questions.stem: A male with insulin dependent diabetes having macular edema develops glaucoma. Which of the following anti-glaucoma drugs should be avoided in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Latanoprost

 

Prostaglandin analogues like latanoprost may aggravate the macular edema in this patient, so should be avoided.

questions.stem: A patient of septic shock was given intravenous nor-epinephrine. The response to this drug is best checked by

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased renal perfusion and reduced urine output

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Increase in mean arterial pressure

 

Ref : Harrison 19th/1761

  • Nor-adrenaline increase systolic as well as diastolic blood pressure and cause bradycardia.
  • The response required in septic shock is increase in blood pressure. Effect of nor-adrenaline is assessed by measuring the mean blood pressure.
  • Target is to increase mean BP above 70 mm Hg and systolic BP above 90 mm Hg.


Harrison 19th/1761

questions.stem: Which of the following diuretics does not require its presence in the tubular lumen for its pharmacological effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Aldosterone antagonists

  •  Most of the diuretics act from the luminal side of the membrane in the nephron.
  • Thiazides, loop diuretics, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors and epithelial Na+ channel blockers (e.g., amiloride and triamterene) are secreted in the proximal tubules through organic anion/ cation transport process.
  • Osmotic diuretics reach the lumen of proximal tubules via glomerular filtration.
  • All these diuretics (thiazides, loop diuretics, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, osmotic diuretics and epithelial Na+ channel blockers) act on the ion channels present on the luminal side of the membranes of nephron.

Aldosterone antagonists like spironolactone do not act through the luminal side rather they act from the basolateral side of the membrane as it acts on the receptors present inside the cells of collecting duct. Therefore, these agents do not require access to the tubular lumen. These are secreted inside the cells of collecting duct from the blood.



ore, these agents do not require access to the tubular lumen. These are secreted inside the cells of collecting duct from the blood.

questions.stem: A 34- year old man with a long history of asthma is referred to pulmonologist. The physician decides to prescribe zileuton. The mechanism of action of this drug is to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Inhibits 5- lipoxygenase

  • 5-lipoxygenase is an enzyme that plays a role in the production of leukotrienes, which are inflammatory mediators that can contribute to the development and progression of asthma. Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase, which helps to reduce the production of leukotrienes and the associated inflammation in the airways, making it a useful drug for the treatment of asthma.
  • Antagonizing leukotriene D4 receptor (option a) is the mechanism of action of drugs such as montelukast and zafirlukast, which are leukotriene receptor antagonists.
  • Inhibiting phosphodiesterase (option c) is the mechanism of action of drugs such as theophylline, which is a bronchodilator and anti-inflammatory agent.
  • Stimulating beta-2 receptors (option d) is the mechanism of action of drugs such as salbutamol and terbutaline, which are short-acting beta-2 agonists used as rescue inhalers for acute asthma exacerbations.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about metformin is not true?

options.label: C
options.text: Can be safely used in patients with renal dysfunction

questions.answerText: Can be safely used in patients with renal dysfunction
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Can be safely used in patients with renal dysfunction

  • In addition to general restrictions for use of oral hypoglycaemics, biguanides are contraindicated in hypotensive states, cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic and renal disease and in alcoholics because of increased risk of lactic acidosis.
  • METFORMIN Decrease hepatic glucose production thereby reducing insulin resistance.
  • It has no effect on insulin secretion by beta cells of pancreas
  • Metformin is the first line drug for type 2 DM and Can be combined with other oral hypoglycaemics like sulfonylureas.
  • Metformin can cause lactic acidosis as an adverse effect. It is contra-indicated in conditions that increase the risk of lactic acidosis. These include:
    • Cardiorespiratory insufficiency (Shock, respiratory disease)
    • Renal dysfunction
    • Liver failure
    • Elderly

questions.stem: Which of the following is an antagonist of a peptide and is used to reduce chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Aprepitant

  • Aprepitant is an antagonist of substance P/neurokinin-1 receptor (NK1 receptor), which is involved in the development of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. By blocking NK1 receptor, aprepitant helps in reducing the incidence and severity of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. It is DOC for delayed vomiting due to chemotherapy.
  • Atrial natriuretic peptide is a hormone that regulates blood pressure and fluid balance.
  • Bradykinin is a peptide involved in the regulation of inflammation and blood pressure.
  • Enalapril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor used to treat hypertension and heart failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Colchicine is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Acts by inhibiting granulocyte migration in the joint.

options.label: C
options.text: It can result in myopathy as an adverse effect.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. All of the above

  • Colchicine is used for treatment of acute attack of gout.
  • It is more effective and faster acting than NSAIDs but is used rarely due to high toxicity.
  • It acts by inhibiting granulocyte migration into the inflamed joint.
  • It causes metaphase arrest (other drugs causing metaphase arrest are vinca alkaloids and taxanes).
  • Most common and dose-limiting toxicity is diarrhea.
  • It can also cause kidney damage, myopathy and bone marrow depression.

questions.stem: A lady who was treated for breast cancer is on long-term tamoxifen therapy as she is ER-positive. Drug tamoxifen can increase the risk for which of the following cancers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Endometrial carcinoma

 

Tamoxifen

  • Tamoxifen was the first selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) to be introduced.
  • Tamoxifen is extensively used in the palliative treatment of breast cancer in postmenopausal women and is approved for chemoprevention of breast cancer in high-risk women.
  • Tamoxifen has estrogen agonistic action on bone and blood. Prevention of the expected loss of lumbar spine bone density and plasma lipid changes consistent with a reduction in the risk for atherosclerosis have also been reported in tamoxifen-treated patients following spontaneous or surgical menopause.
  • However, this estrogen agonist activity on uterus may increase the risk of endometrial cancer.
  • It is a nonsteroidal agent that is given orally.
  • Tamoxifen has an initial half-life of 7–14 hours in the circulation and is predominantly excreted by the liver.
  • Toremifene is a structurally similar compound with very similar properties, indications, and toxicities.

questions.stem: A person is planning a road trip from Chandigarh to Manali. He developed severe vomiting during his last trip to Manali. Which of the following drug should be taken by the person to avoid the motion sickness?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Promethazine

  • DOC for prophylaxis of motion sickness is scopolamine (hyoscine).
  • Alternative drugs that can be used are first generation anti-histaminics due to their anti-cholinergic activity.
  • Promethazine is a first generation anti-histaminic whereas all other drugs mentioned in the options are second generation anti-histaminics.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female with renal disease was admitted for pyelolithotomy. Postoperative analgesic of choice in this patient is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Acetaminophen


All NSAIDs can cause nephrotoxicity due to their propensity to inhibit the formation of PG that cause renal vasodilation.

  • Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is safest NSAID that can be used as analgesic in patients with renal disease. It may be due to its selective action on COX-3.

questions.stemHtml: Based on the mechanism shown in figure. Drug X is likely to be:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Vildagliptin

  • Drug X is a DPP-4 inhibitor like sitagliptin, vildagliptin etc.
  • Pramlintide is an amylin analogue. It is indicated in treatment of both type 1 as well as type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  • Canagliflozin is SGLT-2 inhibitor that acts by causing glucosuria.
  • Exenatide is a GLP-1 analogue that act releasing insulin.
  • Vildagliptin is DPP-4 inhibitor that acts by inhibiting the metabolism of endogenous GLP-1

questions.stem: All of the following are immune check point inhibitors except?
questions.solutionHtml:
tyle="color:black">Ans. C. Cetuximab

 

Explanation:

 

Avelumab, atezolizumab, and durvalumab are all programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) inhibitors that work by blocking the interaction between PD-L1 and its receptor, PD-1, on T cells. This helps to activate the immune system and attack cancer cells.

 

 

 

Cetuximab, on the other hand, is a monoclonal antibody that targets the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) on cancer cells. It does not inhibit PD-L1 and does not work through the same mechanism as PD-L1 inhibitors.

 

Immune Check Point inhibitors

questions.stem: What are the appropriate instructions to be given while prescribing bisphosphonates to a patient?

options.label: A
options.text: To be given empty stomach with a full glass of water

options.label: B
options.text: Must be taken along with food

options.label: C
options.text: Should be stopped if features of gastritis develop

options.label: D
options.text: Should be stopped if bone pains occur

questions.answerText: To be given empty stomach with a full glass of water
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. To be given empty stomach with a glass of water

 

Bisphosphonates

  • They are pyrophosphate analogs.
  • Examples of commonly available bisphosphonates include etidronate, pamidronate, alendronate, risedronate, tiludronate, ibandronate, and zoledronate.

Mechanism of Action

  • They bind hydroxyapatite in bone, inhibiting osteoclast activity.

Clinical Uses

  • Bisphosphonates are DOC for Osteoporosis (Steroid induced, post-menopausal and due to any reason). These are indicated for 5 years and then a drug holiday of 2-3 years is given to avoid adverse effects (increased risk of bone fractures and osteonecrosis of mandible). These can be repeated for another 5 years after drug holiday.
  • DOC for hypercalcemia of malignancy
  • Paget disease of bone.

Side Effects

  • Corrosive esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw.
  • Esophageal irritation can be minimized by
    • Taking the drug empty stomach
    • Taking the drug with a full glass of water
    • Remaining upright for 30 minutes

questions.stem: A patient on digoxin therapy had a level of 1 ng/ml. He was receiving several other drugs and presented 2 months later with flattening of T waves in ECG. Now the plasma level of digoxin is 3.8 ng/ml. Which of the following drug is likely to be responsible?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Clarithromycin


INTERACTIONS OF DIGOXIN

  1. Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and hypercalcemia may precipitate digoxin toxicity.
  2. Drugs causing digoxin toxicity include:
    • Quinidine
    • Verapamil
    • Amiodarone
    • Thiazides
    • Clarithromycin
  3. Renal failure predisposes to digoxin toxicity.

questions.stem: Octreotide is used in all except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Glioma

  • Octreotide is a long-acting somatostatin analog. It can be used: 
    • To decrease secretory diarrhea and other symptoms of carcinoid syndrome and VIPoma.
    • For the management of acromegaly
    • For the treatment of islet cell tumors
    • For controlling acute bleeding due to esophageal varices.
  • DOC for treatment of glioma is temozolomide.
    • To decrease secretory diarrhea and other symptoms of carcinoid syndrome and VIPoma.
    • For the management of acromegaly
    • For the treatment of islet cell tumors
    • For controlling acute bleeding due to esophageal varices.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs block late inward sodium ion channels?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Ranolazine

  • Ranolazine is a late inward sodium channel blocker with mid partial fatty acid oxidation inhibitor property.
  • Trimetazidine is a metabolic modulator that acts as partial fatty acid oxidation inhibitor.
  • Ivabradine is a funny current blocker that result in bradycardiac action.
  • Fasudil is a potent Rho-kinase inhibitor and vasodilator.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the antiarrhythmic agent with the following mechanism of action:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Flecainide

  • The given drug decreased the slope of phase 0 (Na channel blocker) but does not affect the APD (no effect on K channels). These are the properties of class Ic drugs.
  • Class Ic drugs include encainide and flecainide.
  • Tocainide is class I b anti-arrhythmic drug.
  • Procainamide is class Ia drug.
  • Ibutilide is class III anti-arrhythmic drug.

Ans. A. Milnacipran

 

Milnacipran is an SNRI (serotonin noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor) and is used for treatment of depression. All other drugs mentioned in the question are used for treatment of osteoporosis.

 

Drugs Used for Osteoporosis

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female with breast carcinoma is receiving treatment with paclitaxel. During a routine follow-up visit, the patient reports feeling unwell and develops a fever. A complete blood count shows that the patient has a total leukocyte count of 2400/mm3. The healthcare provider suspects that the patient has developed neutropenia, a common side effect of chemotherapy that increases the risk of infections. Which of the following antimicrobial is not suitable for treatment of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Linezolid

 

Linezolid is not suitable for this patient. The reasons are:

  • The patient has immunosuppression, so only bactericidal drugs should be used not bacteriostatic. Linezolid is static whereas beta lactams (meropenem and cefepime) and vancomycin are bactericidal drugs.
  • Linezolid is not commonly used to treat febrile neutropenia.
  • Linezolid causes myelosuppression, hence should not be used in this case because of already low TLC.

Antimicrobial agents commonly used in the treatment of febrile neutropenia:

  • Broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotics, such as cefepime, meropenem, or piperacillin/tazobactam. These antibiotics have activity against a wide range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
  • Aminoglycoside antibiotics, such as gentamicin or tobramycin. These antibiotics have activity against Gram-negative bacteria and are often used in combination with a beta-lactam antibiotic for synergistic effect.
  • Vancomycin. This antibiotic is used to provide coverage against Gram-positive bacteria, particularly in patients with known or suspected infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
  • Antifungal agents, such as fluconazole or voriconazole, may also be used if there is concern for fungal infection.

questions.stem: A patient of bipolar disorder was treated with lithium. Hydrochlorothiazide was prescribed for his hypertension. He developed nausea, vomiting, coarse tremors and brisk reflexes 2 weeks after taking drugs. What is the likely reason for this presentation?

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased metabolism of hydrochlorthiazide by lithium

options.label: C
options.text: Increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium

options.label: D
options.text: Thiazide act as an add on drug to lithium

questions.answerText: Increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium

  • Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic that can increase lithium levels in the body by reducing its renal clearance.
  • This occurs because thiazide diuretics increase sodium reabsorption in the nephron, which can lead to increased lithium reabsorption as well.
  • As a result, lithium levels can rise, leading to symptoms of lithium toxicity, such as nausea, vomiting, tremors, and increased reflexes.

Plasma concentration norms

  • Acute mania: 0.8 – 1.0 mEq/L
  • Prophylaxis: 0.5 – 0.8 mEq/L
  • Toxicity: > 1.5 mEq/L


lexes.

questions.stem: All of the following are adverse effects of amiodarone except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Tachycardia

 

Amiodarone

  • Amiodarone is a broad spectrum anti-arrhythmic drug which belongs to class III of the anti-arrhythmic drugs.
  • Following are the adverse effects:
    • Fall in BP, bradycardia and myocardial depression occurs on IV injection.
    • Photosensitization and skin pigmentation occurs in about 10% of patients.
    • Corneal microdeposits may cause headlight dazzle, but is reversible on discontinuation.
    • Pulmonary fibrosis and alveolitis is most serious side effect seen on prolonged use.
    • Peripheral neuropathy generally manifests as the pelvic and shoulder muscle weakness.
    • Amiodarone interferes with thyroid function and prevents peripheral conversion of T4 to  T3 and causes hypothyroidism

questions.stem: Trimetazidine is a drug approved for treatment of angina pectoris. Its mechanism of action is assumed to be?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Inhibiting mitochondrial LC3-KAT 

 

Trimetazidine

  • This antianginal drug acts by non-haemodynamic mechanisms. There is no effect on determinants of myocardial O2 consumption, such as HR and BP, both at rest as well as during exercise, but angina frequency is reduced, and exercise capacity is increased.
  • In patients not adequately controlled by long-acting nitrate/Beta blocker/CCB, addition of trimetazidine further reduces anginal attacks and increased exercise duration.
  • The mechanism of action of trimetazidine is uncertain, but it may improve cellular tolerance to ischaemia by: Inhibiting mitochondrial long chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (LC3-KAT) a key enzyme in fatty acid oxidation - thereby reducing fatty acid metabolism and increasing glucose metabolism in myocardium.
  • Myocardium uses fatty acid as substrate, thereby have high requirement of O2 (for the same amount of ATP generated by glucose). Since oxidation of fatty acid requires more O2, shift of substrate to glucose would reduce O2 demand.
  • Trimetazidine has been labelled as pFOX (fatty acid oxidation pathway) inhibitor.

Other options:

  • Ivabradine is the bradycardiac agent used in angina. It acts by blocking the funny current in SA node.
  • Fasudil is the rho kinase inhibitor used for angina pectoris.
  • Nicorandil is the K channel opener (with additional NO releasing property) used for angina pectoris.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a fever, headache, and muscle aches. He reports a recent camping trip in a rural area where he was exposed to ticks. On examination, there is a characteristic eschar at the site of a tick bite, as well as regional lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests reveal thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes. Based on the clinical presentation and laboratory findings, the healthcare provider suspects scrub typhus. What is the drug of choice for scrub typhus?
questions.solutionHtml:
>Ans. D. Doxycycline

 

Explanation:

  • Scrub typhus is an acute febrile illness caused by the bacteria Orientia tsutsugamushi, which is transmitted to humans by the bite of infected chiggers. The clinical presentation of scrub typhus is characterized by fever, headache, muscle aches, and the presence of an eschar at the site of the chigger bite. Laboratory findings may include thrombocytopenia, elevated liver enzymes, and leukocytosis.
  • The drug of choice for the treatment of scrub typhus is doxycycline. Other antibiotics, such as azithromycin, chloramphenicol, and ciprofloxacin, may also be used to treat scrub typhus, but doxycycline is the preferred drug due to its effectiveness and low risk of adverse effects.
  • Erythromycin, sulfonamides, and metronidazole are not recommended for the treatment of scrub typhus

questions.stem: Which of the following agents is available as a patch for once-daily use and is likely to provide steady drug levels to treat Alzheimer’s disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Rivastigmine

  • Rivastigmine is a newer reversible anticholinesterase indicated for the treatment of dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.
  • It has better CNS penetration than other drugs of this group.
  • It is the only agent available as a transdermal patch for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
  • It may also be used for dementia associated with Parkinson’s disease.
  • It is applied every 24 hours to improve patient compliance.

questions.stem: Angiotensin receptor blocker which blocks thromboxane A2 receptor is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Losartan

 

Losartan:

  • Competitive antagonist of the thromboxane A2 receptor.
  • Attenuates platelet aggregation.
  • A metabolite of losartan reduces COX-2 mRNA up regulation and COX-dependent prostaglandin generation.

Candesartan:

  • An inactive ester prodrug that is completely hydrolyzed to the active form.

Telmisartan

  • Is a partial agonist of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma.

Olmesartan:

  • Inactive ester prodrug that is completely hydrolyzed to the active form.
  • Clearance is by both renal elimination and biliary excretion.
  • No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild-to-moderate renal or hepatic impairment.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old male with schizophrenia was treated with haloperidol 5 mg once daily at bedtime, which was increased to 7.5 mg daily in the 2nd week and 10 mg daily in the 3rd week. His symptoms improved, but in the 5th week, his family reported that his restlessness had returned, and he kept pacing around in the room, though he was not aggressive. The patient also reported an uncontrollable urge to move around and difficulty in falling asleep. Which of the following drugs would be the best choice for this presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
rong>Ans: A. Propranolol

 

Explanations:

 

The patient's symptoms suggest that he may be experiencing akathisia, a side effect of antipsychotic medications like haloperidol. Akathisia is characterized by restlessness, an uncontrollable urge to move, and difficulty in sitting still.

  • Propranolol, a beta-blocker, is often used to treat akathisia and could be an appropriate choice to address the patient's symptoms.
  • Higher doses of haloperidol may exacerbate the patient's restlessness and are not recommended in this case.
  • Valbenazine is used to treat tardive dyskinesia, a different movement disorder associated with long-term antipsychotic use. It is not indicated for treating akathisia.
  • Dantrolene is a muscle relaxant used to treat muscle spasms and malignant hyperthermia. It is not used to treat akathisia.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a fever, headache, and abdominal pain for the past five days. On examination, his temperature is 102°F (39°C), and he has tenderness in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen. Blood cultures are positive for Salmonella typhi. Which of the following drugs is NOT used in the treatment of enteric fever?
questions.solutionHtml:
ze:12.0pt">Ans. A. Amikacin.

 

Explanation:

  • Enteric fever is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi or Salmonella paratyphi.
  • The mainstay of treatment for enteric fever is antibiotic therapy, which is typically initiated based on the results of a blood culture.
  • Commonly used antibiotics for the treatment of enteric fever include ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, and other fluoroquinolones.
  • Rifampicin is also effective in treating enteric fever and is often used in combination with other antibiotics.
  • However, amikacin, which is an aminoglycoside antibiotic, is not typically used in the treatment of enteric fever.

questions.stem: A patient is operated for bile duct stricture. Post operatively he is receiving 3 ml epidural morphine for pain relief. One day accidentally he received 12 ml of morphine. What will not occur?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Tachycardia

  • Epidural administration of morphine can provide excellent pain relief, but it can also lead to adverse effects such as respiratory depression, urinary retention, hypotension, miosis and pruritus (severe itching). The risk of adverse effects is higher if the patient receives an overdose of morphine.
  • Tachycardia is not a common adverse effect of morphine, and it is not expected to occur in response to an overdose. Rather bradycardia can be seen due to depression of cardiovascular centre in brain.
  • Vomiting and retching are common adverse effects of morphine and can occur with an overdose.
  • Respiratory depression is the most significant adverse effect of morphine and can be life-threatening in severe cases.
  • Urinary retention is another common adverse effect of morphine that occurs due to the inhibition of bladder contractions.
  • Severe itching, or pruritus, is another common adverse effect of morphine that can be bothersome for the patient.

questions.stem: Tramadol acts on µ receptor as an agonist. Additionally, it also acts as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. SNRI

  • In addition to acting as an agonist at the µ-opioid receptor, tramadol also has activity as a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI).
  • This dual mechanism of action provides analgesic effects beyond those produced by opioids alone.
  • Tramadol is not an NDRI (norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor), antihistaminic, or anticholinergic.

questions.stem: Imipenem, an antibiotic with a broad antibacterial spectrum, is co-administered with cilastatin. What is the reason for the same?

options.label: A
options.text: Combination is synergistic against Pseudomonas species

options.label: B
options.text: Cilastatin aids gastrointestinal absorption of active moiety

options.label: D
options.text: Cilastatin inhibits an enzyme in kidney that destroys imipenem

questions.answerText: Cilastatin inhibits an enzyme in kidney that destroys imipenem
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Cilastatin inhibits an enzyme in kidney that destroys imipenem

  • Imipenem is commonly co-administered with cilastatin to prevent the inactivation of imipenem by the renal enzyme dehydropeptidase I (DHP-I) and increase its half-life.
  • Cilastatin is a renal dehydropeptidase inhibitor that prevents the degradation of imipenem in the kidneys, thereby increasing its concentration in the bloodstream and improving its efficacy.
  • Without cilastatin, imipenem would be rapidly metabolized and eliminated by the kidneys, leading to reduced therapeutic efficacy and potentially increased risk of toxicity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a antagonist of PAR-1 receptors of thrombin?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Vorapaxar

  • Vorapaxar is a medication that belongs to the class of drugs known as protease-activated receptor (PAR)-1 inhibitors. It works by selectively blocking the PAR-1 receptor, which is found on the surface of platelets. When PAR-1 is activated by thrombin, it triggers a series of biochemical events that lead to platelet activation and aggregation, ultimately resulting in the formation of a blood clot. By blocking PAR-1, Vorapaxar prevents this process from occurring, thus reducing the risk of blood clots.
  • Prasugrel and Ticlopidine are antiplatelet drugs that act as P2Y12 receptor inhibitors.
  • Tirofiban is a GPIIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor. This group is strongest anti-platelet drugs.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old male had fever for the past 1 week with abdominal distention and loss of appetite. It is not responding to antibiotics and antimalarials. Widal test is negative but RK39 dipstick test is positive. Which of the following drugs can be used in the above patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Liposomal amphotericin B

  • The given symptoms and test results suggest the possibility of visceral leishmaniasis (also known as kala-azar), which is a parasitic disease caused by the Leishmania donovani complex.
  • Out of the options given, the drug that can be used in the above patient is liposomal amphotericin B, which is the recommended first-line treatment for visceral leishmaniasis. Liposomal amphotericin B is a broad-spectrum antifungal medication that is also effective against various parasitic infections, including leishmaniasis.
  • Bedaquiline and Linezolid are antibiotics that are used to treat bacterial infections, and Fluconazole is an antifungal medication that is used to treat fungal infections. None of these drugs are effective against leishmaniasis.
